To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) self-regulation is a limited resource; (2) motivation can overcome ego-depletion effects, and (3) ego depletion is not a loss of motivation.

(a) the self ’s ability to regulate its behavior is limited by the availability of ego resources, (b) ego resources are rooted in the body’s energy stores, (c) the depletion of ego resources leads to a loss of self-regulation, (d) ego depletion can be overcome by strong motivation, and (e) ego depletion is most pronounced in situations that are highly social and that involve social conflict.
self-regulation is a form of self-control, and self-control is an effortful process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of motivational conflicts, especially the conflict between self-interest and the need for social acceptance, in setting the stage for the need to self-regulate.
the interplay between motivation and self-regulatory processes, with the ways in which they can conflict or cooperate, and with the implications of that interplay for understanding human behavior.
the ways that motivation is implicated in self-regulation, and vice versa, as well as the ways that motivation and self-regulatory capacity interact with each other and with each other’s resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
motivation is central to self-regulation, and that self-regulation is central to motivation.
motivation and self-regula- tion are inextricably linked, in many different ways and at many different levels.
self-regulation is the process by which people exert control over their own thoughts, feelings, and actions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strength model of self-regulation is a model of self-control, and self-control is a form of motivation.
self-regulation is the capacity for self-control, which involves the ability to override one’s impulses in order to pursue a different goal.
motivation and self-regulations are two sides of a coin, and they interact with each other in many different ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
motivation is a central factor in self-regulation, and that it is a key variable that must be understood and considered in any theory of self-regulation.
self-regulation is a limited resource, like a muscle that becomes fatigued with use.
motivation plays a key role in the strength model of self-control.
